name: Spit
description: Spit (or 'Slam') is a fast-paced two-player shedding card game related to Speed. Unlike Speed, each player maintains five small 'stock piles' in front of them (similar to Solitaire layout) and races to empty these piles onto two central discard stacks. Play is simultaneous and chaotic. The winner of a round gets to choose the smaller pile for the next round, aiming to start with fewer cards.

overview.description: Spit (or 'Slam') is a fast-paced two-player shedding card game related to Speed. Unlike Speed, each player maintains five small 'stock piles' in front of them (similar to Solitaire layout) and races to empty these piles onto two central discard stacks. Play is simultaneous and chaotic. The winner of a round gets to choose the smaller pile for the next round, aiming to start with fewer cards.

history.origins: Likely developed alongside Speed in the mid-20th century. The name 'Spit' refers to the action of flipping the top card onto the active pile.
history.cultural: Known for the satisfying 'Slap' on the smaller pile at the end of a round.
history.evolution: Spit uses five stock piles per player (1, 2, 3, 4, 5 cards) with top card face up; the related game Speed uses a single face-down stock and a five-card hand per player. Both are competitive patience games with simultaneous play.

setup.players: Two players only. Play is simultaneous with no turns; physical speed and alertness are required to play faster than the opponent.
setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck. Shuffle well and divide the pack equally so each player receives 26 cards; no jokers.
setup.dealing: Shuffle and divide the deck equally (26 cards each). Each player deals five stock piles in a row: first pile 1 card, second 2, third 3, fourth 4, fifth 5. Deal face down then turn the top card of each pile face up. The remaining 11 cards per player stay face down as the spit cards.

rules.objective: Get rid of all your cards. Or have fewer cards at the end.
rules.gameplay: Both players shout 'spit' and flip their top spit card to start two centre spit piles. Play is simultaneous with no turns. Each player may: play a face-up stock card onto either spit pile if it is next in sequence up or down (suit and colour do not matter; ace may play on 2 or king); turn the top card of a stock pile face up; or move a face-up stock card into an empty stock space. When neither can play, both shout 'spit' again and each turns their next spit card onto their pile. When one player empties all stock piles or play is blocked with no spit cards left, players slap to choose a pile; each takes their chosen pile, adds remaining cards, shuffles, and deals a new layout. First to get rid of all cards wins.
keyRules: Play onto a spit pile only if your card is next in sequence up or down; suit and colour do not matter; ace connects to 2 and king.
Only one card may be moved at a time.
When neither can play, both shout 'spit' and each turns the next spit card onto their pile.
First to empty all stock piles wins the round; then players slap to choose which centre pile to take for the next deal.
If a player has fewer than 15 cards they cannot deal a full layout and there is only one spit pile; first to empty stock takes nothing, the other takes the centre.

strategy.basic: Prioritize emptying your Stock Piles because that wins the round. Use empty spots to unbury face-down cards. Play quickly.
strategy.intermediate: Pile Selection: If you are winning, aim to slap the smaller pile so you have fewer cards next round. But sometimes taking a diverse large pile gives you better options for the layout than a tiny pile of specific cards.
strategy.advanced: Two-Handed Play: Use both hands. Lift a card with one hand while flipping a stock card with the other.
tips: Don't cover your piles with your arms.
Slap fast or lose the small pile.

variations.name: Four stock piles
variations.description: Some play with only four stock piles containing one, two, three and four cards each.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant only changes layout size; no engine constant overrides documented in sources.

variations.name: Alternate colour on spit piles
variations.description: Some play that cards on the spit piles must alternate in colour (e.g. on a black 5 only a red 6 or red 4 may be played).
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant adds colour constraint to play; engine overrides not yet mapped from source.
